title: Correctness and expected time of restart
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, $L$ a language of binary strings, and $T$ a natural-number-valued time bound, and suppose $N$ satisfies the aborting decision conditions with time bound $T$. Fix a binary input $x$. Consider the procedure that repeatedly runs $N$ on $x$ in blocks of $T(|x|)$ choices, returning the bit if a block's output is exactly a one-bit string and otherwise continuing. Its expected number of choices, expressed as the sum of its probabilities of not having returned a result through each finite horizon, is at most $2T(|x|)$; moreover, whenever it returns a bit, that bit equals the indicator of whether $x\in L$.

$L$ is a language of binary strings
$N$ satisfies the stated aborting decision conditions with time bound $T$
